header:
Date: 2026-11-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Jake Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Chen (AxiomMed - Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (AxiomMed - Platform), Rohit Singh (AxiomMed - CTO)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20261115-axiommed
summary: POC scoping focused on integration pattern (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs), success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy), workload sizing (5k chats/day + nightly embedding batches), benchmarks (latency p95 target, token cost), and timelines for a 4-week POC culminating in benchmark runs. Customer expressed interest in VPC/private deployment for PHI-sensitive paths but wants to start with hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints for faster time-to-value.
transcript:
[00:00] Jake Martinez: Hey everybody, thanks for joining — we'll kick off, I'm Jake from Redwood, AE, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marta Chen: Hi, all, Marta here. Doing well. Looking forward to this, we've been evaluating a few options so want to get into the nitty gritty.
[00:14] Priya Rao: great, thanks Marta. Quick agenda: POC goals / success criteria, your workloads, recommended deployment paths (hosted vs dedicated vs private), integration examples (SDK + OpenAI compat endpoints), and benchmarks. Then decide next steps.
[00:27] Rohit Singh: sounds good. High level: we want to add a clinical triage chat feature and document summarization pipelines. Primary constraints: PHI, low latency for triage (~ <300ms token latency ideally), and predictable cost.
[00:40] Tom Alvarez: from infra side we'll need to know networking requirements for any VPC peering or on-prem if we go that route. Also curious about function calling because we want structured JSON output to feed downstream systems.
[00:54] Jake Martinez: totally — that's helpful. On success criteria what do you all prioritize? Latency, cost, quality accuracy?
[01:01] Marta Chen: quality and privacy first then latency. If we can meet quality baseline (F1-ish on entity extraction) and keep cost under our threshold we'll be happy.
[01:09] Priya Rao: ok, can I clarify the numbers? You're expecting about 5k interactive chats/day, average session length ~8 turns, average prompt + response ~350 tokens per user turn?
[01:17] Marta Chen: yes that's the ballpark. And nightly embedding jobs for 50k documents, embeddings approximate 1.2M tokens per run.
[01:26] Priya Rao: good. For that workload we typically recommend starting with Redwood hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints for the POC so you can integrate quickly using the same SDK patterns you already have, then iterate to Dedicated or Private if you need isolation or capex predictability.
[01:38] Tom Alvarez: when you say OpenAI-compatible endpoints, is that drop-in API? We have an existing client that calls OpenAI.
[01:44] Priya Rao: yes, it's designed to be drop-in — same request/response shapes, includes function calling semantics and structured output support. We'll share code snippets for Python and Node. There are minor differences for model naming and some header keys but we provide middleware snippets.
[01:57] Rohit Singh: any caveats around streaming? We stream to our UI and need token-level streaming.
[02:03] Priya Rao: streaming supported. We also support chunked KV cache for long context efficiently. There may be tokenization differences for some open models; we'll validate in benchmarks.
[02:14] Marta Chen: on security — we are dealing with PHI; SOC 2 is table stakes, we also need KMS integration and audit logs. What's Redwood's posture there?
[02:22] Jake Martinez: Redwood has SOC 2; we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can be configured with customer KMS in many cases, and we provide audit logs and retention controls. We'll attach the security pack and compliance docs after.
[02:36] Tom Alvarez: good. Network egress — if we start hosted, will any PHI leave our VPC?
[02:42] Priya Rao: hosted option will process in Redwood's environment; we recommend redacting PHI for hosted unless you opt for Private or Dedicated with VPC peering. For the POC you could run non-PHI traffic on hosted and a PHI path on Private later.
[02:54] Rohit Singh: ok that makes sense. Let's talk benchmarks: what metrics should we run and how long will it take?
[03:00] Priya Rao: we typically run: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1k tokens, and quality (accuracy/F1 on your eval prompts). For function calling structured outputs we'll validate schema correctness rate. Benchmark run takes about 1-2 days to collect stable results, plus analysis. We'll need your sample data and a week to provision slots.
[03:22] Marta Chen: timeline wise, we're targeting a 4-week POC to validate integration and run benchmarks, then exec decision. Does that align?
[03:29] Jake Martinez: that's typical. Week 0 - onboarding & sample data, Week 1 - basic integration + smoke tests, Week 2 - benchmark runs, Week 3 - tuning and re-runs, Week 4 - results & exec review.
[03:41] Tom Alvarez: about integration — we'll want SDK examples. Can you walk through a function call + structured output example?
[03:47] Priya Rao: sure, quick example: send a create_task-like function schema in the request; model returns a structured JSON payload; Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint preserves the function_call object. We'll share both streaming and non-streaming examples. Example caveat: sometimes transcription returns 'KV cash' or 'KV cache' spelled weird in auto transcripts but the payload shape remains stable.
[04:10] Marta Chen: will Redwood support automatic rerouting to cheaper model variants on overload? We want a fallback to local smaller model if latency spikes.
[04:17] Jake Martinez: yes, routing policies can fallback by cost tier or latency SLO; for POC we can set a policy to prefer fused LLM for latency-sensitive calls and fall back to more cost-efficient models for background summarization.
[04:29] Rohit Singh: do you have recommendations on quantization or batching settings for our workload?
[04:33] Priya Rao: for interactive triage prioritize latency, so small batch sizes and low-quantization or fp16 for accuracy. For nightly embeddings use high batching and int8/4 quant where possible to reduce cost. Redwood Optimize module can auto-suggest profiles after initial runs.
[04:49] Tom Alvarez: curious about rate limits and concurrency if we go hosted — how do you handle burst traffic?
[04:55] Jake Martinez: hosted supports burst capacity; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput. For the POC we can provision temporary higher bursts. We'll show expected p95 numbers per model.
[05:06] Marta Chen: regarding cost — can you share an example calc? We want cost per 1k messages and monthly estimate.
[05:11] Jake Martinez: yes we'll send a calc. Roughly for our curated model family, at your volume it maps to ~$X per 1k tokens; we'll provide both hosted and dedicated breakouts.
[05:19] Tom Alvarez: about function calling reliability — occasionally we saw hallucinated fields in earlier experiments. How do you surface and test schema conformance?
[05:27] Priya Rao: we run schema conformance tests during benchmarks and measure schema validity rate. For critical fields we suggest validation + lightweight post-processing. Also we can run few-shot prompts to boost correctness.
[05:36] Rohit Singh: any special logging/tracing we get for debug?
[05:39] Jake Martinez: yes per-request traces, token-level timing, model selection logs and full request/response (configurable retention). We can include tracing hooks for your observability stack.
[05:50] Marta Chen: great. For the POC we'll probably start with hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints to validate dev integration fast and then run a dedicated benchmark cluster if results warrant moving to Dedicated/Private.
[06:00] Priya Rao: makes sense. We'll plan benchmarks against the model you select; if you want to try both a Redwood-curated open model and a smaller faster variant we can include both.
[06:10] Tom Alvarez: network setup for VPC peering — what's required from our side?
[06:13] Priya Rao: we'll provide a checklist: CIDR, allowlist IPs, service account, routes, and firewall ports. For on-prem we have an appliance option but that's more involved.
[06:24] Jake Martinez: ok to summarize next steps so everyone has clarity? Priya, can you list the artifacts we'll share?
[06:29] Priya Rao: yes: 1) POC integration checklist and SDK examples (Node + Python) 2) Security pack (SOC2, KMS, audit logs) 3) POC pricing and hosted vs dedicated cost model 4) Benchmark plan + slot proposals
[06:44] Marta Chen: good. We'll upload sample data and a minimal set of eval prompts by Monday.
[06:49] Rohit Singh: and we'll lock down who needs access to benchmark bucket. Tom will coordinate the infra bits.
[06:55] Jake Martinez: perfect. Any final questions or objections?
[06:58] Tom Alvarez: one more, can you share latency numbers p95 for the curated low-latency model? ballpark is fine.
[07:03] Priya Rao: ballpark p95 for 1k token request on low-latency curated model is ~180-320ms depending on region and concurrency. We'll provide concrete numbers in the benchmark doc.
[07:15] Marta Chen: thanks, that's all for now.
[07:18] Jake Martinez: great, we'll follow up with the documents and a proposed benchmark slot. Thanks everyone.
[07:23] (call ends)
